title: Best Podcast Editors and Producers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a podcast editor or producer: what the package should include, how to prepare your audio, price factors and red flags.
intro: A podcast editor turns raw recordings into episodes that are easy to listen to: clean sound, steady levels and no long pauses. Problems usually start before editing, with poor recordings, unclear editing style, or music the show has no right to use. This guide helps you set up a smooth routine with an editor.

faq.q: What is the difference between a podcast editor and a producer?
faq.a: An editor works on the audio: cutting, cleaning and mixing. A producer may also plan episodes, book guests, write show notes and publish. Check which tasks the package covers.

faq.q: How should I send my recordings?
faq.a: Send the original files, ideally a separate track for each speaker, in WAV or a high-quality format. Separate tracks make it much easier to fix one voice without affecting the others.
Decide the style: light editing that keeps the conversation natural, or tight editing that removes filler words and tangents. Tell the editor, and give examples of shows you like.

faq.q: Can the editor add intro music?
faq.a: Yes, but the music must be licensed for podcast use. Ask where it comes from, or supply your own licensed track, so your episodes are not removed or muted later.
Many podcasts now publish video versions and short clips. If you record video, ask whether the package covers video editing and clips, or if that is a separate service.
